title: RASSG: Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating for Streaming Tool Execution
abstract: arXiv:2610.14659v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Streaming speech assistants can launch tools before users finish speaking, overlapping execution with incoming speech to reduce user waiting time. However, subsequent self-corrections can invalidate apparently stable arguments, causing stale execution whose irreversible effects persist even after the final call is corrected. We propose Repair-Aware Semantic Survival Gating (RASSG) to jointly control tool launch and cancellation during streaming speech. RASSG launches a tool when three consecutive speech recognition results arrive with identical nonempty arguments, then combines calibrated argument invalidity risk with execution costs to decide cancellation at the last feasible opportunity before effects become irreversible. Evaluation on ReCAST, FDB-v3, and Audio2Tool uses a controlled execution clock with fixed tool runtimes and cancellation parameters. On ReCAST's prospective-repair subset, RASSG reduces the stale execution rate from L

translated_title: RASSG：面向流式工具执行的修复感知语义生存门控
translated_abstract: 流式语音助手可以在用户尚未说完话时就启动工具，将工具执行与正在进行的语音输入重叠，以减少用户等待时间。然而，用户随后的自我修正可能会使看似稳定的参数失效，导致“过期执行”，即使最终调用得到修正，其不可逆的影响依然会持续存在。我们提出了修复感知语义生存门控，以在流式语音过程中联合控制工具的启动与取消。当连续三次语音识别结果携带相同的非空参数时，RASSG 启动工具；随后将经过校准的参数失效风险与执行成本相结合，在影响变得不可逆之前的最后一个可行时机决定是否取消。评估在 ReCAST、FDB-v3 和 Audio2Tool 上进行，采用受控执行时钟，并固定工具运行时间与取消参数。在 ReCAST 的前瞻性修正子集上，RASSG 将过期执行率从 L（原文此处截断）
tldr: RASSG 通过在连续三次语音识别结果一致时才启动工具，并结合参数失效风险与执行成本在影响不可逆之前决定取消，从而降低流式语音助手中的过期执行率。
en_tdlr: RASSG gates tool launch until three consecutive identical ASR results with nonempty arguments, then combines calibrated argument-invalidation risk with execution costs to cancel at the last feasible moment, reducing stale executions in streaming speech assistants.
